summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of Addison’s disease presented with fatigue, leg cramps, nausea, salt craving, and headache following a recent viral illness. She had increased her prednisone during the illness but did not adjust her fludrocortisone. In the emergency department, she was found to have hyperkalemia, hyponatremia, and acute kidney injury due to hypovolemia, consistent with an adrenal crisis. She was treated with IV fluids, stress-dose hydrocortisone, and kayexalate. Her electrolytes normalized, kidney function improved, and symptoms resolved. Prednisone was continued at 10 mg daily with a plan for outpatient tapering, while fludrocortisone was briefly increased and then returned to baseline. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to taper steroids, hold amlodipine until PCP follow-up, and resume her usual medications.
